data.content:
Implementation plan (complexity: high; provider trust boundary plus transactional cache application):
1. Land only after knots-2af8 exposes schema-v22 transactional generation-apply APIs, knots-c472 exposes authenticated GitHub submission identity, and knots-74e2/knots-9b6a expose live provider policy and protected-ref contracts. Treat their shipped interfaces as authoritative and adapt this plan without weakening the trust boundary.
2. Add a provider-neutral authenticated-read interface and sealed evidence types, likely under src/replication/provider/. The raw adapter result must bind provider kind, stable repository identity, policy identity/version, trusted integration or service identity, legacy-freeze state, protected ref names, exact control/canonical/archive/inbox OIDs, observation time or provider revision, and freshness bounds. Keep ValidatedProtection construction private to validation of this evidence.
3. Implement GitHub readback through authenticated API calls: read repository identity, applicable rulesets and bypass actors, exact protected refs/OIDs, and retained signed proposal/inbox heads. Reject role bypasses, missing trusted Actions integration, incomplete rule coverage, paginated omissions, stale ETags/revisions, renamed repositories, and any policy/ref mismatch. Fetch commit/tree/blob bytes only by returned immutable OIDs; never checkout or execute fetched content.
4. Implement Diffinite readback through its authenticated control surface: read stable repository identity, installed receive-policy version/digest, service capability identity, freeze marker, exact protected refs/OIDs, and credential-scoped retained inbox heads. Reject permissive rollback-floor state, actor-ID substitution for credential ID, missing service-only control ownership, stale policy revisions, and mismatched refs. Fetch bytes by immutable OID through the provider-supported authenticated transport.
5. Add an orchestrator that performs two-phase validation: read and validate policy/control facts; fetch exact control, canonical generation, archive descriptors/packs, and retained inbox delta by OID; validate hashes and control/vector relationships; then re-read policy and control and require the same policy revision plus exact control OID. Any race or mismatch returns a typed fail-closed result before invoking SyncService.
6. Connect the validated fetch result to the schema-v22 SyncService boundary from knots-2af8. Exercise fresh bootstrap and incremental paths, including exact-once retained delta, watermark advancement, writer-vector state, cache tiers, and lease-quarantine preservation. Keep provider discovery outside the SQLite transaction; pass only fully authenticated, immutable, hash-verified input into transactional application.
7. Define offline behavior explicitly. Git local-only and legacy sync continue on their existing non-v2 path. A repository configured for protected v2 with an unavailable, unsupported, or unauthenticated provider returns a clear retryable/fail-closed result and leaves refs, files, and SQLite unchanged. Tracked markers, remote URLs, Git config, and fetched repository content cannot mint protection authority.
8. Add deterministic GitHub and Diffinite adapter fixtures covering pagination, freshness, policy rollback, identity substitution, stale/missing OIDs, mid-fetch races, corrupt bytes, and retained-inbox gaps. Add disposable live probes using existing approved rails to compare adapter evidence with provider readback and prove ordinary credentials cannot mutate protected refs.
9. Add bootstrap/incremental integration matrices and actual prior-client compatibility coverage. Assert all failure paths preserve SQLite checksums/watermarks/quarantine and all legacy/archive/generation/pack/event/inbox/Git objects. Run focused tests, cargo fmt/check/test, size and coverage gates, then make sanity.
10. Commit imperatively, attach the sneka-agents note, push a codex branch, open and merge the authorized GitHub PR after CI, verify origin/main exactly, and advance this Knot through implementation/review/shipment under fresh e2e leases.

Ownership: this Knot owns authenticated provider discovery, exact immutable reads, freshness/CAS validation, and invocation of the shipped schema-v22 apply boundary. It does not reimplement provider write enforcement, signed proposal creation, generation construction, bridge cutover, destructive retention, production PostgreSQL, or new infrastructure. No later operator approval gate exists inside this scope.
